evidence.why: Shows the selected table and 0x4000 predicate.
Shows identifier exclusion, matching filters, and bounded output.

facts.rationale: The predicate body and candidate loop establish the data flow; reading Toy_80304CC8 corrects the baseline's mistaken ownership interpretation.
facts.value: Receives an integer trophy identifier and returns whether 0x4000 is set in its context-selected packed u16 entry. The candidate-building loop requires this predicate, excludes the input identifier and language-excluded identifiers, requires matching display-group and classification values, and appends passing identifiers up to the supplied maximum. Its separate Toy_80304CC8 check is not an ownership check.

facts.rationale: Uses the verified registration and callback sequence without asserting an unverified user-facing Collection-room mapping or treating mask 7 as a single callback pass.
facts.value: Serves as the main-camera render callback installed by Toy camera setup. After successful camera activation, it conditionally installs an erase color and clears the camera's projected color region, dispatches enabled GX-link lists with mask 7 (callback passes 0, 1 and 2), applies null fog, and finalizes deferred camera drawing.

evidence.why: Generation stamping and the scheduler's skip comparison.

facts.rationale: Preserves the supported lifecycle while replacing the inaccurate activation interpretation with the scheduler implementation's generation-stamp behavior.
facts.value: When both the retained light archive and active light GObj are present, removes the old object's processes and process-link object, clears its slot, and resolves the requested replacement symbol from that archive. Otherwise loads TyLight.dat and retains the returned archive. A successful lookup creates and registers a light GObj. If the loaded list reports animation, installs _Toy_80306C5C and stamps the object's processes with the current scheduler generation, suppressing execution during the remainder of that traversal. Without animation, installs no update process. A missing symbol reports the requested label and asserts.

evidence.why: Animation helper roles and complete panel-label construction.
Archive initialization and subsequent panel-loader call.

facts.rationale: The archive handle and resource-name table are separate inputs. The caller establishes the localized viewer archive, so the prior TyLight-archive attribution should be corrected.
facts.value: Replaces the active indexed panel-label display. Resolves the selected joint and its joint, material and shape animation exports from the already loaded archive in ToyGlobalsS_.x50, constructs the JObj hierarchy, requests frame zero and registers the new GObj for rendering. The inspected viewer setup populates this archive slot from TyMnView.dat or TyMnView.usd.

evidence.why: Exact signature and normal completion are explicit.

facts.rationale: Distinguishes a void return type from non-returning control flow.
facts.value: Signature: void(void). A parameterless initializer that returns no value and communicates its results through shared-state writes.

evidence.why: Shows the complete parameterless void reset.

facts.rationale: Preserves the established type while removing misleading no-return terminology.
facts.value: Signature: void(void). A parameterless initializer that returns no value; its outputs are mutations of Toy global storage.

evidence.why: Shows the full data flow and linking block outside the successful-load guard.

facts.rationale: Retains directly expressed byte-address operations without asserting a compiled struct layout, and corrects the false successful-load-only linking model.
facts.value: Traverses a null-terminated LightList pointer array and loads each descriptor. Successful loads clear the indexed byte at base+0xDC+index, optionally attach the first animation list and request frame zero, set that byte for a position animation, and capture position and interest at base+0x1C+index*0xC and base+0x7C+index*0xC, where base comes from Toy_sbss_804D6ED4. Only successful loads advance the index. The optional aggregate output starts at zero and becomes one when animation is attached. Linking executes for every input entry, including failed loads: it assigns prev->next when prev is non-null, otherwise assigns first, then replaces prev with the load result. A failure can truncate the chain and a subsequent success can replace first; empty input leaves first uninitialized.

evidence.why: Allocation guards, formatting writes, and unconditional SIS assignments.

facts.rationale: Corrects the per-field allocation implication while preserving the confirmed input-to-text flow.
facts.value: Reads the display singleton and saved-language setting, lazily creates x144 and x148 independently, and creates x14C and x150 together when x14C is NULL. Created HSD_Text pointers and formatting are retained. Every call derives four language-sensitive SIS indices from the supplied trophy ID and installs them on the four cached objects.

facts.rationale: The paired final allocation explicitly contradicts four independent guards.
facts.value: Uses three initialization guards for four text objects: x144 and x148 each have their own NULL guard, while the x14C NULL guard creates and configures both x14C and x150. Existing formatting is preserved when the corresponding guard is false. All four SIS contents are refreshed on every call; there is no independent x150 repair path.

evidence.why: Descriptors, object construction, camera attachments, and process registration.
Context identifiers and diagnostic mask override.

facts.rationale: Distinguishes the six presentation objects from the four explicit camera attachments and three distinct descriptors.
facts.value: Loads the authored ScMenFigure camera descriptor and uses two static perspective descriptors to construct four CObjs attached to main, frustum, secondary, and light-camera GObjs; the authored descriptor is reused for the light camera. Two additional GObjs initialize screen layers. Six GObj handles, four SisLib context identifiers, callback registrations, and render masks are retained in Toy global state. Mode flags select the frustum-camera update process and optionally replace normal masks with the diagnostic frustum mask.

facts.rationale: Preserves exact initialization and branch precedence without misidentifying the alternate viewer as the editor-entry mode.
facts.value: Sets x61 to 0, x60 to 4, and x58 to 0x95E, and calls _Toy_80307828(0). The frustum camera receives _Toy_8030B530 when _Toy_sbss_804D6EA2 is nonzero, otherwise _Toy_8030E110 when _Toy_sbss_804D6E50 is nonzero, otherwise _Toy_80309404. Independently, nonzero _Toy_sbss_804D6E50 clears the other five presentation masks and sets the frustum mask to 0x02A0000000000000. This alternate-viewer flag is distinct from the _Toy_sbss_804D6EA0 state that selects the nine-row parameter editor.
